quiz.title: CBSE Class 12 Maths 2003 Paper Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight board-level questions in the style of the 2003 paper, spanning calculus, matrices and determinants, vectors, 3D geometry and probability. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: The derivative of tan x with respect to x is:
questions.explanation: d/dx (tan x) = sec<sup>2</sup> x is a standard result. Note that sec x tan x is the derivative of sec x, not tan x.

questions.q: The matrix | k 2 ; 3 6 | is singular when k equals:
questions.explanation: A matrix is singular when its determinant is 0. Here 6k − 6 = 0, so k = 1.
Since d/dx (tan x) = sec<sup>2</sup> x, the integral of sec<sup>2</sup> x is tan x + C.

questions.q: If two non-zero vectors a and b are parallel, then a × b is:
questions.explanation: |a × b| = |a||b| sinθ. For parallel vectors θ = 0, so sinθ = 0 and the cross product is the zero vector.

questions.q: The distance between the points (2, 3, 1) and (2, 3, 6) is:
A fair die is rolled once. The probability of getting a prime number is:
questions.explanation: The primes on a die are 2, 3 and 5 — three outcomes out of six, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.q: ∫ from 0 to π/2 of cos x dx equals:
questions.explanation: ∫ cos x dx = sin x. Evaluating from 0 to π/2 gives sin(π/2) − sin 0 = 1 − 0 = 1.

questions.q: For any square matrix A, the matrix A + A<sup>T</sup> is always:
questions.explanation: (A + A<sup>T</sup>)<sup>T</sup> = A<sup>T</sup> + A = A + A<sup>T</sup>. A matrix equal to its own transpose is symmetric.

faq.q: What does the CBSE Class 12 Maths 2003 paper cover?
faq.a: It follows the Class 12 syllabus of that year — differentiation and integration, matrices and determinants, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, differential equations and probability. That spread still forms the backbone of the board paper today.

faq.q: Is the 2003 paper still worth solving for the current exam?
faq.a: Yes. The pattern has changed — today's paper adds MCQ and case-study sections — but the underlying concepts are the same. The 2003 paper offers clean, well-set questions that are excellent for strengthening fundamentals.

faq.q: How is the 2003 paper different from a recent CBSE paper?
faq.a: The 2003 paper uses the older marking scheme with mostly short- and long-answer questions and no objective or case-based section. Use it for concept practice, then switch to a recent sample paper to rehearse the current format.

faq.q: What is the best way to practise with a previous-year paper?
faq.a: Attempt it in one timed sitting without notes, mark it against the answer key, then re-solve only the questions you got wrong. That gap analysis teaches far more than reading solved answers straight through.
